questions.questionHtml:

Statement: No student of Class X failed the science exam this year.

Conclusions:

I. The science exam was very easy.

II. All students of Class X passed science.
questions.solution:
Statement: 'No student of Class X failed' means every student of Class X passed.

Conclusion I: Says the exam was very easy. This is a possible reason for everyone passing, but it does not necessarily follow — students may have worked hard, been well prepared, etc. So I does not follow.

Conclusion II: Says all students of Class X passed science. This is the direct logical complement of 'no one failed'. So II follows.

Hence only Conclusion II follows.

questions.question: Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option. Statement: Although recent advancements in quantum computing have significantly improved processing speeds, the stability of quantum states remains a critical barrier to developing large-scale quantum computers for practical applications. Assumptions: I. Quantum computing holds the potential for faster data processing than classical computing. II. Quantum states are inherently unstable, making large-scale quantum computing unfeasible. III. Recent advancements in quantum computing have resolved the issue of quantum state stability.
questions.questionHtml:
Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option.

Statement: Although recent advancements in quantum computing have significantly improved processing speeds, the stability of quantum states remains a critical barrier to developing large-scale quantum computers for practical applications.

Assumptions:

I. Quantum computing holds the potential for faster data processing than classical computing.

II. Quantum states are inherently unstable, making large-scale quantum computing unfeasible.

III. Recent advancements in quantum computing have resolved the issue of quantum state stability.

options.text: Only I and II are implicit
Only II and III are implicit
All I, II and III are implicit
options.html: All I, II and III are implicit

questions.solution:
Assumption I: The statement says quantum computing has improved processing speeds — implying it can be faster than classical computing. Implicit.

Assumption II: The statement explicitly calls stability of quantum states 'a critical barrier' to large-scale practical quantum computers — i.e., current instability makes large-scale quantum computing unfeasible for now. Implicit.

Assumption III: The statement says stability 'remains' a critical barrier — i.e., the issue has not been resolved. So III is the opposite of what the statement says. Not implicit.

Hence only I and II are implicit.

questions.questionHtml: In Bhakti traditions, which two broad types of worship are mentioned?
questions.solution:
The Bhakti movement is classically divided into two broad streams:

Saguna bhakti — devotion to a deity with form and attributes (e.g., Rama, Krishna), as practised by Tulsidas, Surdas, etc.

Nirguna bhakti — devotion to a formless, attribute-less Divine, as practised by Kabir, Guru Nanak, Ravidas, etc.

options.text: Restricted songs to temples and priests only
options.html: Restricted songs to temples and priests only

options.text: Focused only on melody, not on social reform
options.html: Focused only on melody, not on social reform

questions.solution:
Annamacharya (1408–1503) was a Telugu saint-composer of Tirupati who composed about 32,000 'sankirtanas' (devotional songs) in praise of Lord Venkateshwara.

His songs combined intense devotion with social messages of equality, criticising caste discrimination.

He did not restrict songs to temples and priests; he sang for everyone — kings, common people and devotees alike.

Hence the best description is that he wrote over 32,000 songs promoting devotion and equality.

questions.question: Why can hockey players use only the flat, left-hand side of the stick?
questions.questionHtml: Why can hockey players use only the flat, left-hand side of the stick?

options.text: Better control and reduced injury risk
Prevents uneven bounce, ensures uniform rebound
Mandated right-hand play for training ease

questions.solution:
Under the rules of field hockey, players are allowed to play the ball only with the flat (left-hand) side of the stick.

This rule exists because hitting with the rounded side would cause the ball to deflect unpredictably; restricting play to the flat side ensures a uniform, predictable rebound.

'Better control and reduced injury risk' is a side benefit, not the rule's stated purpose.

The rule does not address left-handed advantage and does not 'mandate right-hand play for training ease'.

Hence the correct reason is: it prevents uneven bounce and ensures a uniform rebound.

questions.solution:
The Regulating Act of 1773 elevated the post of Governor of Bengal to that of 'Governor-General of Bengal' and provided for a council of four members to assist and check him.

Decisions in the council were taken by majority vote, with the Governor-General having a casting vote.

The Act did not make him report directly to the Crown, did not reduce him to a ceremonial role, and did not transfer the post to Madras.

Hence the correct change is option 3.

questions.question: In which type of geological formation are gorges most commonly developed?
questions.questionHtml: In which type of geological formation are gorges most commonly developed?
questions.solution:
A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep, almost vertical sides, formed when a river cuts downward much faster than the valley sides erode sideways.

This kind of vertical erosion happens mainly when the rock on the sides is hard and resistant — the river can only cut downward, not widen the valley.

Soft sediment and glacial till erode laterally easily and form wider valleys.

Volcanic ash is loose and does not support vertical cliffs typical of gorges.

Hence gorges develop most commonly in hard rocks.

questions.solution:

Hence the correct definition is: It is the difference between the birth rate and the death rate.

questions.question: What is the primary function of telomerase enzyme?
questions.questionHtml: What is the primary function of telomerase enzyme?
questions.solution:
Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein enzyme that adds repetitive nucleotide sequences (TTAGGG in humans) to the ends of chromosomes (telomeres).

This lengthening of telomeres compensates for the gradual shortening that occurs with each round of DNA replication.

DNA replication is done mainly by DNA polymerases; DNA repair involves different enzymes; RNA transcription is performed by RNA polymerase.

Hence the primary function of telomerase is telomere lengthening.

questions.question: Which of the following commissions recommended the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council to institutionalize Centre–State cooperation?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following commissions recommended the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council to institutionalize Centre–State cooperation?
questions.solution:
The Sarkaria Commission on Centre–State Relations (1983–88) recommended setting up a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263, with its own permanent secretariat, to institutionalise consultation between the Union and the States.

On its recommendation, the Inter-State Council was set up in 1990.

The Rajamannar Committee was a Tamil Nadu state-level committee; the Punchhi and Venkatachelliah commissions dealt with later issues.

Hence the correct answer is the Sarkaria Commission.

questions.question: Why are cooking utensils often made with a copper bottom?
questions.questionHtml: Why are cooking utensils often made with a copper bottom?

options.text: Copper is a good insulator, preventing heat loss
options.html: Copper is a good insulator, preventing heat loss

options.text: Copper has a low melting point, making it easy to manufacture
options.html: Copper has a low melting point, making it easy to manufacture

options.text: Copper is a good conductor of heat, ensuring even heating
options.html: Copper is a good conductor of heat, ensuring even heating

options.text: Copper reacts readily with food, enhancing flavour
options.html: Copper reacts readily with food, enhancing flavour

questions.solution:
Copper has very high thermal conductivity (among the best of common metals).

A copper bottom therefore distributes heat quickly and evenly across the base of the utensil, preventing hot spots and ensuring food cooks uniformly.

Copper is not an insulator; its melting point is fairly high (~1084 °C), so ease of manufacture is not the reason; and food contact with copper is actually limited (which is why copper utensils are usually tinned or used only at the bottom).

Hence the correct reason is: copper is a good conductor of heat.

questions.solution:
A Uniform Civil Code (envisaged under Article 44 of the Constitution as a Directive Principle) aims to provide one set of personal laws — covering marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, maintenance, etc. — applicable to all citizens of India, irrespective of their religion.

Criminal law is already uniform under the BNS / IPC and CrPC / BNSS.

Tax laws and administrative procedures are governed under separate frameworks.

Hence the primary objective of UCC is option 3.

questions.question: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) provides support for?

questions.solution:
The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), launched in 2020, is a medium-/long-term debt financing facility for investment in post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.

Supported projects include cold storages, warehouses, pack-houses, grading and sorting units, primary processing units — i.e., agri-logistics and cold chains.

It does not give free fertilizers, cash transfers, or fund MGNREGA work.

Hence the correct option is Agri-logistics and cold chains.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Under India's updated State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC) for 2025, which sector received the highest budgetary allocation for climate adaptation?
questions.questionHtml: Under India's updated State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC) for 2025, which sector received the highest budgetary allocation for climate adaptation?
questions.solution:
Under India's updated State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCC) for 2025, the largest share of climate-adaptation funding has been allocated to agriculture and water resources.

These sectors are the most climate-sensitive in India — farmers and water availability bear the immediate brunt of rainfall variability, droughts and heatwaves.

Transport, urban planning and renewable energy are largely on the mitigation side and received smaller shares.

Hence the correct option is Agriculture and Water Resources.

It does not focus only on raw material exports; it does not import final products to fill domestic demand; and it serves both export and large domestic markets.

questions.questionHtml: The budget for a construction project is allocated to land acquisition, building materials, and labor in the ratio 5 : 3 : 2. During the project, the cost of land acquisition rose by 5%, building materials rose by 10%, and labor fell by 20%. What is the percent change (increase or decrease) in the total project cost?
questions.solution:
Take the ratio as actual amounts: land = 5, materials = 3, labor = 2 (total = 10).

New amounts:

Land: 5 × 1.05 = 5.25

Materials: 3 × 1.10 = 3.30

Labor: 2 × 0.80 = 1.60

New total = 5.25 + 3.30 + 1.60 = 10.15.

Change = +0.15 on a base of 10 = +1.5%.

Hence the cost rose by 1.5%.

questions.question: In a city, the current number of literate people is 25,000. If the number of literate males decreases by 5% and the number of literate females increases by 10%, the total literate population becomes 25,250. What is the present number of literate males in the city?
questions.questionHtml: In a city, the current number of literate people is 25,000. If the number of literate males decreases by 5% and the number of literate females increases by 10%, the total literate population becomes 25,250. What is the present number of literate males in the city?
questions.solution:
Let literate males = m and literate females = f.

m + f = 25,000 …(i)

After change: 0.95m + 1.10f = 25,250 …(ii)

From (i): f = 25,000 − m. Substitute in (ii):

0.95m + 1.10(25,000 − m) = 25,250

0.95m + 27,500 − 1.10m = 25,250

−0.15m = −2,250

m = 15,000.

Hence the current number of literate males = 15,000.

questions.question: A baker ordered 10 kg of premium flour and some additional kg of standard flour. The price of premium flour per kg was twice that of the standard flour. Due to an ordering error, the quantities of the two types of flour were interchanged. This decreased the total cost by 25%. Find the ratio of the quantity of premium flour to standard flour in the original order.
questions.questionHtml: A baker ordered 10 kg of premium flour and some additional kg of standard flour. The price of premium flour per kg was twice that of the standard flour. Due to an ordering error, the quantities of the two types of flour were interchanged. This decreased the total cost by 25%. Find the ratio of the quantity of premium flour to standard flour in the original order.
questions.solution:
Let standard flour price = p per kg, so premium = 2p per kg.

Let original quantity of standard flour = q kg (premium = 10 kg).

Original cost = 10(2p) + q·p = (20 + q) p.

Interchanged cost = q(2p) + 10·p = (2q + 10) p.

New cost is 25% less:

(2q + 10) p = 0.75 (20 + q) p

2q + 10 = 15 + 0.75 q

1.25 q = 5

q = 4.

Ratio premium : standard = 10 : 4 = 5 : 2.

questions.question: A trader sells one brand of tea at ₹150 per kg, incurring a 25% loss. He also sells another brand of tea at ₹200 per kg, incurring a 20% loss. If he mixes the two brands in equal proportions and sells the mixture at ₹175 per kg, what is his overall profit or loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: A trader sells one brand of tea at ₹150 per kg, incurring a 25% loss. He also sells another brand of tea at ₹200 per kg, incurring a 20% loss. If he mixes the two brands in equal proportions and sells the mixture at ₹175 per kg, what is his overall profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
CP of Brand 1 per kg = 150 / 0.75 = ₹200.

CP of Brand 2 per kg = 200 / 0.80 = ₹250.

Take 1 kg of each (equal proportions):

Total CP = 200 + 250 = ₹450.

Total SP = 2 × 175 = ₹350.

Loss = 450 − 350 = ₹100.

Loss% = (100 / 450) × 100 ≈ 22.22%.

questions.question: From a 64-liter container of pure spirit, 8 liters are removed and replaced by water. This operation is performed a total of three times. What is the final quantity of spirit remaining in the container?
questions.questionHtml: From a 64-liter container of pure spirit, 8 liters are removed and replaced by water. This operation is performed a total of three times. What is the final quantity of spirit remaining in the container?
questions.solution:
Each time, 8 / 64 = 1/8 of the spirit is removed, leaving (1 − 1/8) = 7/8 of the spirit.

After 3 such operations: spirit = 64 × (7/8)³ = 64 × 343/512 = 343/8 = 42.875 ≈ 42.88 liters.

questions.question: A juice vendor mixes water with pure orange juice. If he sells the mixture at the cost price of pure orange juice and makes a profit of 20%, what is the ratio of water to pure orange juice in the mixture, respectively?
questions.questionHtml: A juice vendor mixes water with pure orange juice. If he sells the mixture at the cost price of pure orange juice and makes a profit of 20%, what is the ratio of water to pure orange juice in the mixture, respectively?
questions.solution:
Let cost of 1 L of pure juice = p; he sells 1 L of mixture at p with 20% profit.

So CP of 1 L mixture = p / 1.20 = 5p/6.

Let mixture contain x L water + 1 L pure juice. Total water has zero cost, so total cost = p.

CP per litre of mixture = p / (x + 1) = 5p / 6

→ x + 1 = 6/5

→ x = 1/5.

Ratio water : pure juice = (1/5) : 1 = 1 : 5.

questions.question: A car covers 40% of a certain distance at a pace of 20 km/h and the remaining distance at a pace of 30 km/h. What is the average speed of the car for the entire journey?
questions.questionHtml: A car covers 40% of a certain distance at a pace of 20 km/h and the remaining distance at a pace of 30 km/h. What is the average speed of the car for the entire journey?
questions.solution:
Let total distance = D.

Time for first 40% = 0.4 D / 20 = D/50.

Time for remaining 60% = 0.6 D / 30 = D/50.

Total time = 2D / 50 = D / 25.

Average speed = total distance / total time = D / (D/25) = 25 km/h.

questions.question: A and B are jogging around a park's circular track which has a perimeter of 1.2 km. They start from the same point at 6:00 a.m. and run in opposite directions. A's speed is 5 km/h, and B's speed is 7 km/h. At what time will they meet for the fifth time?
questions.questionHtml: A and B are jogging around a park's circular track which has a perimeter of 1.2 km. They start from the same point at 6:00 a.m. and run in opposite directions. A's speed is 5 km/h, and B's speed is 7 km/h. At what time will they meet for the fifth time?
questions.solution:
When running in opposite directions, relative speed = 5 + 7 = 12 km/h.

Time for first meeting = 1.2 / 12 hours = 0.1 hour = 6 minutes.

Each successive meeting also occurs every 6 minutes (they together cover one lap in 6 min).

For the 5th meeting: 5 × 6 = 30 minutes after 6:00 AM.

So they meet at 6:30 AM.

questions.question: Which of these lines is parallel to 3x + 2y = 5?
questions.questionHtml: Which of these lines is parallel to 3x + 2y = 5?
questions.solution:
Two lines are parallel iff they have the same slope, i.e. the coefficients of x and y are proportional.

3x + 2y = 5 has the direction (3, 2).

Only 3x + 2y = 7 has the same coefficient pair (3, 2), so it is parallel.

2x + 3y = 5, 3x − 2y = 5 and x + y = 5 have different slopes.

Hence the parallel line is 3x + 2y = 7.

questions.questionHtml: If sin(90° − x) = cos(2x), then what is x?
questions.solution:
sin(90° − x) = cos x.

So the equation becomes cos x = cos 2x.

This is satisfied when 2x = x (i.e. x = 0) within the principal range.

Check: cos 0° = 1 = cos 0° ✓.

For x = 30°: cos 30° ≈ 0.866, cos 60° = 0.5 — not equal.

For x = 25°, 15°: also unequal.

Hence x = 0°.

questions.solution:
All three sides of triangle ABC are equal to the corresponding three sides of triangle XYZ.

The congruence rule that uses three pairs of equal sides is SSS (Side-Side-Side).

SAS uses two sides + included angle; ASA uses two angles + included side; AAS uses two angles + a non-included side.

Hence the rule is SSS.

questions.question: Given A and B are complementary angles, and sin A = 3/5, what is tan B?
questions.questionHtml: Given A and B are complementary angles, and sin A = 3/5, what is tan B?
questions.solution:
If A and B are complementary, A + B = 90°, so B = 90° − A.

tan B = tan(90° − A) = cot A = cos A / sin A.

Given sin A = 3/5, by Pythagoras cos A = 4/5 (3-4-5 triple).

cot A = (4/5) / (3/5) = 4/3.

Hence tan B = 4/3.

questions.question: Select the correct option: Only after a decade of fieldwork ___ fully grasp the dialect's nuances.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

Only after a decade of fieldwork ___ fully grasp the dialect's nuances.
questions.solution:
The sentence opens with the restrictive adverbial 'Only after a decade of fieldwork', which forces subject-auxiliary inversion in the main clause.

The verb 'grasp' is in the base form, so the past simple inverted form 'did she + grasp' is required.

'Only after a decade of fieldwork did she fully grasp the dialect's nuances.'

Normal-order forms ('she had', 'she did') break the required inversion; 'had she' would be used only with a past-perfect main verb.

Hence the correct option is 'did she'.

questions.question: Select the correct option: The professor's remarks were so dense with jargon that they bordered on ___.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

The professor's remarks were so dense with jargon that they bordered on ___.
questions.solution:
After the preposition 'on' we need a noun, not an adjective or a non-existent word.

Opacity (noun) = the quality of being hard to understand. ✓

Opaque is an adjective.

Opacus is not standard English in this context.

Opalescent (adj.) refers to a milky iridescence, not unclarity.

Hence the correct option is Opacity.

questions.question: Select the correct option: Her rebuttal, though eloquent, failed to ___ the central issue raised by the opposition.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

Her rebuttal, though eloquent, failed to ___ the central issue raised by the opposition.
questions.solution:
To 'address' an issue means to deal with it directly. The sentence says her rebuttal failed to deal with the central issue.

Digress means to wander off topic — would not collocate with 'failed to'.

Circumvent means to go around / avoid — but 'failed to circumvent' would actually mean she did not avoid the issue, which contradicts the intended sense.

Elude means to escape from / evade — wrong context.

Hence the correct option is 'address'.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The reforms being recommended by the panel (1)/ are not only intended to streamline administrative functions (2)/ but also addressing the asymmetries in resource allocation (3)/ that have long plagued rural districts. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The reforms being recommended by the panel (1)/ are not only intended to streamline administrative functions (2)/ but also addressing the asymmetries in resource allocation (3)/ that have long plagued rural districts. (4)
questions.solution:
The correlative 'not only … but also …' demands parallel structures on both sides.

In part (2) the structure is 'intended to streamline' (to + base verb).

In part (3) the structure is 'addressing the asymmetries' (gerund), which breaks parallelism.

It should read 'but also (intended) to address …'.

Hence the error is in part (3).

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: What the committee failed to deliberate on adequately (1)/ were not the policy's objectives themselves, (2)/ but the political ramifications it (3)/ might have had if implemented without broader consensus. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

What the committee failed to deliberate on adequately (1)/ were not the policy's objectives themselves, (2)/ but the political ramifications it (3)/ might have had if implemented without broader consensus. (4)
questions.solution:
The subject of the verb is the noun-clause 'What the committee failed to deliberate on adequately' — singular.

A singular subject requires a singular verb (was, not were).

Part (2) uses 'were not the policy's objectives themselves'; it should be 'was not the policy's objectives themselves' (the subject 'What' is singular).

Parts (1), (3) and (4) are grammatically correct.

Hence the error is in part (2).

Rare minerals are known to have been secretly extracted from the site by unauthorized workers before the inspection.

questions.solution:

Option 4 changes the structure and tense.

Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.question: Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage: For seventeen-year-old Meera, adolescence was not merely a phase of hormonal transitions and academic aspirations — it became an arena where perception and self-worth collided with insidious intensity. In a world saturated with curated digital aesthetics and algorithm-driven beauty hierarchies, Meera's own reflection began to feel less like truth and more like betrayal. Every scroll through her social media feed deepened a gnawing dissonance: between her authentic self and the impossible silhouettes idolized online. This wasn't mere teenage insecurity — it manifested as a systematic devaluation of her physical self. Gradually, she adopted punitive behaviours: food became conditional, mirrors became adversaries, and compliments transformed into cryptic reminders of inadequacy. The subtle descent into dysmorphia was neither loud nor linear. Academically capable and socially pleasant, Meera wore the mask of normalcy with precision. Yet beneath the practiced smiles was a quiet implosion. She began withdrawing emotionally, rationalizing her distress as vanity, and trivializing her worth. The turning point came not with drama, but with silence — a refusal to eat for days, which led to medical intervention. Therapeutic engagement introduced her to the concept of self-image distortion, and the emotional scaffolding required to rebuild her fractured sense of identity. Through sustained counseling, Meera disentangled societal impositions from intrinsic value. She began to internalize that beauty is not a monolith dictated by culture but a spectrum shaped by diversity, health, and self-compassion. Meera's narrative is not a singular anomaly but a mirror to a larger epidemic — where teenagers battle unspoken wars behind flawless digital façades. Combating this requires more than awareness; it calls for critical media literacy, empathetic environments, and systemic redefinition of beauty norms that extend beyond superficial metrics. questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: I suggested that he goes to the doctor immediately.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

I suggested that he goes to the doctor immediately.

options.text: should have go to the doctor

questions.solution:
After verbs of suggestion ('suggested') in the subjunctive, the verb in the that-clause should be in the base form.

So 'he goes' must be replaced by 'he go'.

The complete corrected sentence: 'I suggested that he go to the doctor immediately.'

Option 1 drops the article 'the' before 'doctor' and changes the adverb.

Option 2 keeps the incorrect 'goes'.

Option 4 uses 'should have go' (incorrect form).

Hence option 3 ('go to the doctor immediately') is correct.

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: I am used to get up early in the morning.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

I am used to get up early in the morning.
questions.solution:
The structure 'be used to' (meaning 'be accustomed to') is followed by a gerund (-ing form), not the base verb.

So 'to get up' must become 'to getting up'.

Corrected sentence: 'I am used to getting up early in the morning.'

Options 1, 2 and 4 either keep the base form, change the preposition, or use the wrong preposition.

Hence option 3 ('to getting up early') is correct.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech. She said, "He doesn't listen to me."
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

She said, "He doesn't listen to me."

options.text: She said he don't listen to her.
options.html: She said he don't listen to her.

options.text: She said that he doesn't listened to her.
options.html: She said that he doesn't listened to her.

options.text: She said that he didn't listen to her.
options.html: She said that he didn't listen to her.

options.text: She said that he didn't listened to her.
options.html: She said that he didn't listened to her.

questions.solution:
Reporting verb 'said' is past, so the present-tense verb 'doesn't listen' shifts back to 'didn't listen'.

The pronoun 'me' (in her speech) becomes 'her' in reported speech.

Correct reported form: 'She said that he didn't listen to her.'

Option 1 uses 'don't' with a singular subject (incorrect).

Option 2 keeps the present tense 'doesn't' and uses the wrong 'listened'.

Option 4 uses 'didn't listened' (double past — incorrect).

Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The manager informed the employees that the deadline for submission had been extended by two days.

options.text: "You may submit the work two days later than planned," the manager informed.
options.html: "You may submit the work two days later than planned," the manager informed.

options.text: "The deadline has been extended by two days," said the manager.
options.html: "The deadline has been extended by two days," said the manager.

options.text: "We are extending the submission deadline by two days," the manager said.
options.html: "We are extending the submission deadline by two days," the manager said.

options.text: "You must finish it within two extra days," the manager said.
options.html: "You must finish it within two extra days," the manager said.

questions.solution:
Reverse the back-shift: past perfect 'had been extended' goes back to present perfect 'has been extended' in direct speech.

The reported clause 'that the deadline for submission had been extended by two days' becomes the direct quote 'The deadline has been extended by two days'.

Attribution: 'said the manager'.

Correct: '"The deadline has been extended by two days," said the manager.'

Option 1 paraphrases and changes the agent voice.

Option 3 changes tense to present continuous and meaning.

Option 4 changes the meaning entirely.

Hence option 2 is correct.

1. These narratives often explore the ethical and social consequences of technological advancement, from artificial intelligence to genetic engineering.

2. Science fiction is a genre of speculative fiction that typically deals with imaginative concepts such as futuristic science and technology.

3. This makes it a powerful tool for social commentary and for anticipating future challenges and dilemmas.

4. While entertaining, the genre serves a purpose beyond mere escapism.
questions.solution:
Sentence 2 introduces the topic — defines science fiction.

Sentence 4 makes a general claim — that the genre serves a purpose beyond entertainment.

Sentence 1 illustrates that purpose by stating what these narratives often explore.

Sentence 3 concludes with 'This makes it a powerful tool', referring to the exploration in 1.

Logical order: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3.
